sample.txt: This sighting provides evidence that decades of conservation and restoration are transforming one of New York City's most iconic waterways. The otter was photographed by a motion-activated camera deployed by local scientist, RJ Hawkins. (2/4)

Hawkins is conducting long-term camera trap monitoring for wildlife along the river as part of a program managed by the zoo’s Education Dept. The discovery is the first documented occurrence of a river otter in the Bronx section of the Bronx River since the early 1900s. (3/4)

They once ranged throughout NY's waterways but disappeared from many areas due to pollution, habitat degradation, & unregulated trapping. Today they are considered indicators of healthy freshwater ecosystems as they depend on clean water, abundant fish, & intact habitats. (4/4)
